oil.summary: Brent cratered 4.61% today to $73.53/bbl, extending a brutal month that has now wiped nearly 29% off the front contract. The dominant driver is the US-Iran sanctions détente: Washington granted Tehran a 60-day oil sanctions waiver through 21 August, with nuclear inspectors returning and an MOU reportedly in place. The prospect of stranded Persian Gulf barrels re-entering global supply is overwhelming bulls, despite a supportive 6.1-million-barrel draw in US crude inventories for the week ending 19 June. RBOB bore the brunt intraday, off 6.36%, while heating oil was relatively insulated at -2.05%. VLCC spot earnings spiked near $470,000/day as importers scramble for tonnage, but that is a logistical response, not a price floor. CME options now price a 77% probability of an OPEC production cut at the next meeting, signalling the market expects the group to defend prices.
drivers: US grants Iran 60-day oil sanctions waiver, opening Persian Gulf barrels to India and global markets and weighing heavily on Brent and products
EIA reports a large 6.1-million-barrel US crude inventory draw, providing only partial offset to the bearish supply backdrop
OPEC options market prices 77% probability of a production cut at next meeting, reflecting producer-side alarm at the sharp month-long selloff

gas.summary: Henry Hub and TTF diverged sharply today. Henry Hub gained 3.30% to $3.251/MMBtu, sustaining an 11.83% monthly rally, while TTF fell 2.06% to €41.15/MWh and is down 15.47% on the month. The European softness aligns with Qatar's prime minister signalling that LNG exports could return to normal production within weeks following disruptions tied to the Hormuz crisis — a direct supply-restoration signal for Atlantic Basin markets. On the US side, the Trump administration moved to cut red tape for oil and gas drillers on federal lands, a medium-term bearish supply signal, while Trump separately ordered a price-gouging probe at fuel stations. Petronas reported a new offshore gas discovery in Suriname, though near-term market impact is limited.
drivers: Qatar PM signals LNG exports could normalise within weeks, pressuring TTF lower as European supply anxiety eases
Henry Hub outperforms on domestic demand dynamics; Trump administration's deregulation push for federal-land drilling adds a medium-term supply overhang
Trump orders price-gouging investigation at retail fuel stations, adding political headline risk for downstream gas and fuel prices

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs held relatively stable at $76.41, down a marginal 0.21% on the day and up 3.50% on the month, decoupling from TTF's sharp monthly decline. Power sector news flow was dominated by structural longer-term themes: Adani Group announced a target of 10 GW of nuclear capacity in India by 2035, and India separately reported cutting coal imports as domestic coal output and renewables expansion reduce reliance on seaborne fuel. Nine North Sea nations including the UK formalised a clean energy and offshore power collaboration. An AI power demand piece flagged electricity infrastructure as the key investable theme of the current cycle. The euro sinking to a one-year low on falling oil prices raises ECB rate-cut expectations, which could ease financing costs for European clean-energy investment.
drivers: EUA prices hold firm despite TTF weakness, supported by structural clean-energy policy signals including the nine-nation North Sea offshore power initiative
Adani targets 10 GW Indian nuclear capacity by 2035; India cuts coal imports as domestic supply and renewables expand — both reshaping long-run power generation mix
Euro hits one-year low as oil-price disinflation fuels ECB rate-cut bets, potentially lowering cost of capital for European power and infrastructure projects
